ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, society, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family, and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of organizing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, then in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government of Pesisir Selatan Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in the Regional Government of South Coastal Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.

Article 24

(3) In the event that the implementation of integrated services is conducted through networking, UPTD PPA shall be responsible for the entire referral process of services needed by women and children experiencing problems.

Article 67
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) Supervision conducted by Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD Leaders in accordance with their duties and functions are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

3. The results of supervision and evaluation serve as evaluation material for women's empowerment and child protection program policies.
(4) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) in order to realize the objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 67
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards, by facilitating the formation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
b. technical guidance and training, including:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities, Regional Government provides facilities, means and infrastructure in implementing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari caring for women and children;
e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) Supervision conducted by Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD Leaders in accordance with their duties and functions are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation, the Regent may appoint OPD in accordance with their duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation serve as evaluation material for women's empowerment and child protection program policies.
(4) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) in order to realize the objectives of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.

9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).

16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Article 24
(1) The implementation of UPTD PPA services shall be integrative in nature, either in the form of one-stop or networked services to provide optimal services to women and children experiencing problems.

(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

Article 29

a. assist women and child victims of acts of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(3) Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and

a. women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems can resume their social life; and b. women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

(4) The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include: a. their lives are threatened;

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by the promotive aspect is to improve so that health status becomes increasingly improved, for example the provision of early breastfeeding initiation (IMD) and exclusive breastfeeding which can help increase immunity to disease because of colostrum and nutrients contained in breast milk, so that children are not easily affected by disease.
Letter b What is meant by the preventive aspect is to prevent from contracting disease or to keep healthy people to remain healthy, for example washing hands before eating and after defecating will prevent the occurrence of diarrheal disease.
Letter c What is meant by the curative aspect is the process of curing a person from a state of illness physically and psychologically.
Letter d What is meant by the rehabilitative aspect is the process of maintaining so that a person who has recovered (not yet 100% recovered) returns to being fit as before.

b. empower women and children experiencing criminal and/or civil problems to determine their future; c. provide moral support to women and children experiencing criminal and/or civil problems in facing the process they are undergoing; and
d. make women and children experiencing criminal and/or civil problems feel accepted in the community environment. (2) Counseling services are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of:
a. counselors;
b. psychologists; and/or
c. psychiatrists.
(3) Counseling services are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort and confidentiality of information from women victims of acts of violence.
(4) Stages of counseling services include:
a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling;
c. case discussion; and
d. site visits.

Article 27
Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by the promotive aspect is to improve so that health status becomes increasingly improved, for example the provision of early breastfeeding initiation (IMD) and exclusive breastfeeding which can help increase immunity to disease because of colostrum and nutrients contained in breast milk, so that children are not easily affected by disease.
Letter b What is meant by the preventive aspect is to prevent from contracting disease or to keep healthy people to remain healthy, for example washing hands before eating and after defecating will prevent the occurrence of diarrheal disease.
Letter c What is meant by the curative aspect is the process of curing a person from a state of illness physically and psychologically.
Letter d What is meant by the rehabilitative aspect is the process of maintaining so that a person who has recovered (not yet 100% recovered) returns to being fit as before.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by health rehabilitation carried out comprehensively is health rehabilitation carried out in a promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative manner and able to respond.
Paragraph (3) Letter a What is meant by medical services is services provided to reduce impact and prevent further injury, suffering and cost threats. includes:
1. physical examination and treatment of physical injuries;
2. treatment of psychological disorders;
3. treatment for prevention of sexually transmitted diseases;
4. treatment for prevention of HIV; and

Article 24
(1) The implementation of UPTD PPA services shall be integrative in nature, either in the form of one-stop or networked services to provide optimal services to women and children experiencing problems.

Article 53
(1) Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
(2) Regional governments provide educators for inclusive education at every education unit.

Article 53
Paragraph (1) What is meant by children with disabilities and special needs are children who experience limitations/exceptionalities whether physical, mental-intellectual, social, or emotional that significantly influence their growth and development process compared to other children of the same age.
What is meant by formal education is systematic, structured, tiered activities starting from elementary school to higher education and their equivalents, including academically and generally oriented study activities, specialization programs, and professional training conducted on a continuous basis.
What is meant by non-formal education is an educational pathway outside formal education that can be implemented in a structured and tiered manner.
What is meant by informal education is the pathway of family education (tutoring, home schooling, private) and environment. Education is organized by providing exemplary models, building willingness, and developing the creativity of students in the learning process.
What is meant by inclusive education is an educational service system that includes children with special needs learning together with their peers in regular schools closest to their place of residence.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently Clear.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, society, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family, and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of organizing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, then in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government of Pesisir Selatan Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in the Regional Government of South Coastal Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Child rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
General

Article 30
(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
(2) The provision of safe house services aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include: a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 31
(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.

Article 53
(1) Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
(2) Regional governments provide educators for inclusive education at every education unit.

6.2.text:
Article 33
(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems to their place of origin.
(2) Repatriation of women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 32
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
(3) Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(4) The Regional Government shall provide legal aid to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(5) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so on.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 of 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, society, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing the life of the nation and state.

Parents, family, and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of organizing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in national level laws and regulations, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as the improvement of the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, then in providing protection to women and children, the Regional Government of Pesisir Selatan Regency needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.

Article 30
(1) Regional Governments may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
(2) The provision of safe house services aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include: a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 53
(1) Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, non-formal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
(2) Regional governments provide educators for inclusive education at every education unit.

Article 35
UPTD PPA implements the repatriation and social reintegration of women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 34
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems can resume their social life; and b. women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 28
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter c is intended to restore and develop the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil matters to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) In the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or social community organizations that already exist.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with UPTD PPA.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit in the Regional Government of South Coastal Regency.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Child rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

Article 61
(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.
(2) The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices; b. all work that exploits, provides, or offers Children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that exploits, provides, or involves Children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

Article 31
(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.

Letter e What is meant by assistance is all actions taken in the form of complaint services, health services, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with UPTD PPA.

Article 32
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil problems against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
(3) Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(4) The Regional Government shall provide legal aid to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(5) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.
